cards.front: In mechanics, what is a mathematical model?
cards.back: A simplified version of a real-world situation used to make mathematics manageable.

cards.front: When using a particle model, the object's mass is treated as [ ___ ].
cards.back: When using a particle model, the object's mass is treated as concentrated at a single point.

cards.front: What three physical properties are ignored when an object is modelled as a particle?
cards.back: SizeShapeRotation / turning effects

cards.front: Why might a particle model be unsuitable for a car in a turning maneuver?
cards.back: It cannot account for tilting, spinning, or forces acting on different parts of the car.

cards.front: What is the definition of constant acceleration?
cards.back: The rate of change of velocity remains the same throughout the motion.

cards.front: What two conditions must be met to use SUVAT (constant-acceleration) equations?
cards.back: Acceleration is constantMotion is in a straight line

cards.front: Near the Earth's surface, the acceleration due to gravity ($g$) is taken as $\text{[...]}$.
cards.back: Near the Earth's surface, the acceleration due to gravity ($g$) is taken as $\boxed{9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}}$.

cards.front: If 'upwards' is the positive direction, what is the value of acceleration for an object in free fall?
What does it mean for an object to move freely under gravity?
cards.back: The only force acting on the object is its weight.

cards.front: When is the assumption of negligible air resistance likely to be unsuitable?
cards.back: When the object has a large surface area relative to its mass (e.g., a feather or parachute).

cards.front: If air resistance is ignored in a model, how will the calculated final speed of a falling object compare to its real speed?
cards.back: The calculated speed will be higher than the real speed.

cards.front: A [ ___ ] surface has no friction, while a rough surface includes friction.
cards.back: A smooth surface has no friction, while a rough surface includes friction.

cards.front: A smooth surface has no friction, while a [ ___ ] surface includes friction.
cards.back: A smooth surface has no friction, while a rough surface includes friction.

cards.front: What is assumed about a light object (like a string or rod) in a mechanics model?
cards.back: It has zero mass and its weight is ignored.

cards.front: What is the physical consequence of modelling a string as inextensible?
cards.back: Connected objects have the same magnitude of acceleration (if the string is taut).

cards.front: For connected objects to share the same acceleration magnitude, the inextensible string must be [ ___ ].
cards.back: For connected objects to share the same acceleration magnitude, the inextensible string must be taut.

cards.front: What is the consequence of modelling a pulley as smooth and light?
cards.back: The tension in the string is the same on both sides of the pulley.

cards.front: State three assumptions made when an object is modelled as a rod.
cards.back: Mass is concentrated along a lineIt has no thicknessIt is rigid (does not bend)

cards.front: A rod is assumed to be [ ___ ], meaning it does not bend.
cards.back: A rod is assumed to be rigid, meaning it does not bend.

cards.front: A rod is assumed to be rigid, meaning it does not [ ___ ].
cards.back: A rod is assumed to be rigid, meaning it does not bend.

cards.front: Why is the particle model suitable for a small parcel sliding a long distance?
cards.back: The parcel's size is small compared to the distance travelled and it does not rotate.

cards.front: How should you justify the suitability of a model in an exam?
cards.back: Identify the modelling assumption and link it to a specific physical effect in the real situation.
